method: Original authored control surfaces for crown and visor; closed 5944-triangle LOD0 with a real open eye slit, 24 through-holes, closed separate brass trim and padded liner. Hidden high-detail cages retain non-destructive modifiers in Blender. Existing rejected neural helmet is only a proportion reference, never the production surface.
materials: Original generated steel, brass and navy-cloth tiles only. Continuous angular UVs have one rear integer-tile seam. Steel samples source steel-512.png at exact crop [96,96,160,160], mirror-composes the source pixels, then area-resamples 2x to a 64x64 tile; physical repeat .035 m and roughness .53. This removes the source broad lighting band without painted colors, synthetic grain or a new external texture.
rig: Reuse the project's original PortraitChest/PortraitHead motion; new rigid helmet parts follow Head, lower collar follows Chest. No third-party mesh, rig or motion.
scope: One original helmet and collar candidate, with old torso shown as unfinished context. Full character, hands, full-body motion and runtime integration remain separate unfinished requirements.
gates: Readable original crown, narrow actual eye slit, clean continuous visor/rim and real breathing holes in front/side/back views
No source-face mask fragments, melted visor or triangular trim edge
Editable authored cage retained in Blender and real exported GLB inspected
Original portrait animation preserved and actual browser poses match Blender at five marker frames
No visible collar collision during the original head turn

review.root_independent_review: accepted as a full-body assembly component
review.findings: UV patch seams eliminated; silhouette, eye slit and breathing apertures readable; no visible gorget penetration in reviewed pose.
review.limits: Component approval only. Full character runtime approval and actual assembled WebGL motion remain separate.
